penalties_applied.name: not_legitimate_or_grey
penalties_applied.reason: Acting as an anonymous payment proxy for third-party services (Kagi, Brave) almost certainly violates those services' terms of service, which prohibit account sharing or resale. It also creates serious AML/KYC legal exposure when deliberately obscuring the identity of payers from merchants. This is legally and operationally grey at best, and likely not viable.

rationale: The underlying desire — paying for privacy tools without linking one's identity — is real, but any solo-operator service that acts as a payment intermediary to obscure buyer identity from the merchant violates those merchants' ToS and triggers AML/KYC regulatory obligations that a solo operator cannot legally bear. Even if the idea were clean, the buyer is a diffuse global consumer segment paying $2–3/month, which requires B2C scale to be viable. The not_legitimate_or_grey penalty applies, effectively disqualifying this.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for a solo non-technical operator. Building a payment proxy that anonymises subscribers from Kagi or Brave would violate those services' terms of service and potentially money-transmission laws. There is no compliant, buildable version of this micro-service.
notes: Fails not_legitimate_or_grey gate (ToS violation + AML exposure). Also fails operational_autonomy (2), buildability_with_ai (3), and buyer_clarity (4) build gates. Drop.
